claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Live-CLI revalidation on 2026-09-30 — this run's runner has the `claude` CLI installed and `claude --version` reports `2.1.286 (Claude Code)`, matching the target exactly. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.281 to **2.1.286** together (no divergence), covering five releases (2.1.282–2.1.286) in one pass. Reviewed every changelog entry across that range for catalog surface. Adopted/documented: **`claude plugin install --config <server>.<key>=<value>`** (2.1.285), which sets a bundled `.mcpb` MCP server's own settings at install time so it starts without a manual `/plugin` → Configure visit — directly relevant to `headhunter`, whose Gmail/Calendar/Notion/Todoist integrations are exactly the kind of bundled MCP server this targets; documented in the install guide's Useful-flags section and its What-you-get row. **`claude plugin configure <plugin>`** (2.1.285), which shows a plugin's options and which are unset, or saves new values read from stdin with `--values-stdin` — documented alongside it as the inspect/non-interactive-set pairing, and noted in `docs/agent-guidelines/security.md` as the preferred way to set a bundled MCP server's secrets over typing them where shell history could capture them. **`claude plugin validate` marketplace/plugin-name check** (2.1.283): a `marketplace.json` entry naming a plugin or marketplace Claude Code cannot actually install now fails validation instead of passing silently — re-ran `claude plugin validate --strict .` against this catalog's own manifest, which still passes clean (all three entries use plain lowercase-hyphen names). **`claude plugin validate` `outputStyles`/`themes`/`monitors`/`lspServers` path check** (2.1.283): catches a plugin declaring one of those paths missing or outside its own directory — this catalog ships no `plugin.json` of its own (checked via repo-wide `find`), so the check has no surface here directly, but it was run against all three listed plugin repos as an audit (read-only clones; no findings — none of the three declare `outputStyles`, `themes`, `monitors`, or `lspServers`). **`claude plugin marketplace add` replace-notice** (2.1.284): now says when it replaces a marketplace already added under the same name from a different source, and how to undo it — documented as a new troubleshooting row, since a `Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` GitHub add and a manually-cloned local add would otherwise silently clobber each other with no explanation before 2.1.284. Reviewed and found no catalog surface: the 2.1.282 `claude plugin uninstall` settings-file-safety fixes (stops and names the file instead of silently deleting saved options/secrets when the settings file is unreadable or still enables the plugin) — host-lifecycle hardening with no manifest change, noted as a troubleshooting row only; the 2.1.283 `claude plugin details` MCP-server-count fix for plugins declaring servers in `plugin.json` (this catalog's manifest declares no MCP servers of its own); `claude plugin marketplace remove` now listing which installed plugins it removed (host UX, no manifest surface); the 2.1.283 plugins-with-no-`version` restored-at-newest-commit fix (all three catalog plugins already have no `version` field and already track their source branch head — behavior is unchanged, not newly exposed); the 2.1.284 `sparsePaths` marketplace-cloning-empty fix on older git (this catalog's manifest sets no `sparsePaths`); the 2.1.284 failed-first-install dependency-version-range fix (this catalog's only cross-marketplace dependency, `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn: [superpowers-dev]`, has never hit this path in review); the 2.1.285 plugin/marketplace-install-over-SSH `GIT_SSH`/`core.sshCommand` fix and the `claude plugin disable`/`enable` case-mismatch settings fix (this catalog's own name and all three plugin names are already consistently lowercase); the 2.1.285 'why a git address is refused' and git-URL-validation error-message improvements (this catalog's sources are the credential-free `github`+`repo` shorthand, never a raw URL); and the 2.1.286 marketplace-refuse-to-load error now naming why instead of 'not found' (documented as a refinement to the existing 'Marketplace file not found' troubleshooting row) and the npm-source dependency-install restriction (this catalog uses only `github` sources, never `npm`, per AGENTS.md). Platform-specific (VSCode/Windows/web/Claude Tag/Code Review) and host/session/UI-only entries across 2.1.282–2.1.286 (Sonnet 5.5 default, permission-prompt/list/scrollbar polish, retry/fallback/auth fixes, Remote Control, sandbox, vim mode, etc.) have zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`, 3 plugins in sync, no drift), `make validate-skills` (`claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills`), `scripts/check-platform-targets.sh --assert-current`, and `claude plugin validate --strict .` on the marketplace manifest all pass clean against the live 2.1.286 CLI. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, and `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` needed no schema change across the whole 2.1.282–2.1.286 range. Only Claude Code entries in this shared platform-target file were touched; Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode values are untouched. Prior verification (2026-09-23): 2.1.281 was confirmed live and reviewed for the 2.1.280 → 2.1.281 delta (the `claude plugin update` scope-resolution fix and the hook/MCP `claude plugin validate` checks, both documented) — see the install guide's per-version sections for full history.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
